retrievalTopK.title: Masks, fit and honest expectations
retrievalTopK.text: A well-fitting respirator labelled N95 filters at least 95 percent of the most penetrating particle size under test conditions. Real protection also depends on the seal. Cloth masks vary greatly. A mask is a last layer, after staying indoors in cleaner air.
tags: mask n95 fit filtration outdoor protection

retrievalTopK.title: Cooking, heating and carbon monoxide
retrievalTopK.text: Cooking and unflued heating can dominate indoor particle exposure. Use a lid, extract fumes outside where safe, and never burn charcoal, kerosene or biomass in living space without a flue. Carbon monoxide has no smell; a detector and fresh air are essential.
tags: cooking stove kerosene biomass carbon monoxide safety

retrievalTopK.title: Why indoor air can be worse
retrievalTopK.text: Indoor particles come from outside air that leaks in and from sources such as cooking and unflued combustion. A steady-state mass balance is used: outdoor air enters, particles deposit or are removed by a purifier, and indoor sources add mass. A correctly sized purifier and one closed room reduce the space you have to clean.
tags: indoor home mass balance cooking windows purifier

retrievalTopK.title: Climate emissions and local smoke are different
retrievalTopK.text: A car trip emits climate-warming CO2 and also produces local pollutants. Walking and cycling have no operational emissions. Official CO2e factors quantify the climate effect; local pollutant effects are described qualitatively here because a single universal gram-per-kilometre figure is not available.

retrievalTopK.text: A well-fitting respirator labelled N95 filters at least 95 percent of the most penetrating particle size under test conditions. Real protection also depends on the seal. Cloth masks vary greatly. A mask is a last layer, after staying indoors in cleaner air.

retrievalTopK.title: Cooking, heating and carbon monoxide
retrievalTopK.text: Cooking and unflued heating can dominate indoor particle exposure. Use a lid, extract fumes outside where safe, and never burn charcoal, kerosene or biomass in living space without a flue. Carbon monoxide has no smell; a detector and fresh air are essential.

retrievalTopK.title: Why indoor air can be worse
retrievalTopK.text: Indoor particles come from outside air that leaks in and from sources such as cooking and unflued combustion. A steady-state mass balance is used: outdoor air enters, particles deposit or are removed by a purifier, and indoor sources add mass. A correctly sized purifier and one closed room reduce the space you have to clean.

retrievalTopK.title: Climate emissions and local smoke are different
retrievalTopK.text: A car trip emits climate-warming CO2 and also produces local pollutants. Walking and cycling have no operational emissions. Official CO2e factors quantify the climate effect; local pollutant effects are described qualitatively here because a single universal gram-per-kilometre figure is not available.

tags: cooking stove kerosene biomass carbon monoxide safety

retrievalTopK.title: Why indoor air can be worse
retrievalTopK.text: Indoor particles come from outside air that leaks in and from sources such as cooking and unflued combustion. A steady-state mass balance is used: outdoor air enters, particles deposit or are removed by a purifier, and indoor sources add mass. A correctly sized purifier and one closed room reduce the space you have to clean.
tags: indoor home mass balance cooking windows purifier

retrievalTopK.title: When to open the windows
retrievalTopK.text: Open windows when outdoor air is cleaner than indoor air. Almanair uses a simple sun-position calculation to constrain that window around solar noon, then compares modelled outdoor and indoor concentrations. On a severe inversion day there may be no good window at all.
tags: ventilation windows noon outdoor indoor timing

retrievalTopK.title: How Almanair reads the air
retrievalTopK.text: Almanair combines your own reading with a simple model of your day. Every number has a source and an uncertainty range. Nothing here is a medical diagnosis.

retrievalTopK.title: Sizing a purifier for a room
retrievalTopK.text: Match the clean-air delivery rate to the room. In SI units clean air changes per hour equal the purifier's cubic metres per hour divided by the room's cubic metres. A higher rate cleans faster; a filter only works if the room is closed and the fan actually runs.

retrievalTopK.title: Cooking, heating and carbon monoxide
retrievalTopK.text: Cooking and unflued heating can dominate indoor particle exposure. Use a lid, extract fumes outside where safe, and never burn charcoal, kerosene or biomass in living space without a flue. Carbon monoxide has no smell; a detector and fresh air are essential.

retrievalTopK.title: Why indoor air can be worse
retrievalTopK.text: Indoor particles come from outside air that leaks in and from sources such as cooking and unflued combustion. A steady-state mass balance is used: outdoor air enters, particles deposit or are removed by a purifier, and indoor sources add mass. A correctly sized purifier and one closed room reduce the space you have to clean.

retrievalTopK.title: When to open the windows
retrievalTopK.text: Open windows when outdoor air is cleaner than indoor air. Almanair uses a simple sun-position calculation to constrain that window around solar noon, then compares modelled outdoor and indoor concentrations. On a severe inversion day there may be no good window at all.

retrievalTopK.title: Reading the air without panic
retrievalTopK.text: An AQI band tells you how cautious to be, not exactly how you will feel. Use the band with your own plan: who is sensitive, how long you will be outside, and whether you have a filtered room. The WHO 24-hour PM2.5 guideline is 15 micrograms per cubic metre; it is a guideline, not a safe threshold.

retrievalTopK.title: When to open the windows
retrievalTopK.text: Open windows when outdoor air is cleaner than indoor air. Almanair uses a simple sun-position calculation to constrain that window around solar noon, then compares modelled outdoor and indoor concentrations. On a severe inversion day there may be no good window at all.

retrievalTopK.title: Climate emissions and local smoke are different
retrievalTopK.text: A car trip emits climate-warming CO2 and also produces local pollutants. Walking and cycling have no operational emissions. Official CO2e factors quantify the climate effect; local pollutant effects are described qualitatively here because a single universal gram-per-kilometre figure is not available.
